main_body: Bonsai-style pine tree: three leaf canopy clumps (large upper, right, left lower) on a diagonal brown trunk
top_band: Canopy tops: lighter green clumps at rows ~1-8 with mid/dark greens below; organic foliage mass with lit upper surface and darker underside, not a flat cap
evidence: Organic tree: foliage clumps read as rounded volumes with lighter tops and darker undersides, and the trunk sits beneath them. The canopy tops are lit and the undersides shaded, so it works as a 3/4 organic form, even though it is a side-on silhouette in style. There is no flat architectural elevation and no receding side face.

style.evidence: The canopy uses about 4 greens with some mottled clumping, and the outline is a dark green-tinted tone next to the leaves, with a dark purple-brown outline on the trunk. The trunk is fairly flat: mostly 2-3 browns with a thin highlight and little bark grain. Compared with the references, which have many leaf clumps in 5-6 greens and detailed bark and roots, the candidate is simpler and thinner. The canopy masses are broad and smooth, with few distinct leaf clusters or highlights. It is a plausible stylized bonsai, but a careful artist would see it as lower in density than the reference next to it.
